faq.question: What kinds of businesses do you work with?
faq.answer: We work with SMBs and enterprises, with a particular focus on US agencies and B2B service firms. Our experience spans healthcare, commerce, manufacturing, data publishing, and professional services. The starting point is the problem and the delivery needs, rather than a single industry.

faq.question: Can you build a complete application, not just an automation?
faq.answer: Yes. Our work includes customer-facing AI products, internal applications, data platforms, and integrations. We scope the product, interfaces, infrastructure, and ongoing engineering together.

faq.question: Do we need to replace our existing tools?
faq.answer: We start with the systems you already use. Integrations can connect them; custom software fills gaps where existing tools do not fit the workflow.

faq.question: Who owns the software and how is it handed over?
faq.answer: Ownership, access, and third-party licenses are agreed in the engagement scope. Our delivery approach includes documentation, a walkthrough, and an operating runbook so your team can understand and operate the system.

faq.question: How do you handle sensitive data and AI decisions?
faq.answer: We scope access, deployment, data handling, and approval requirements before building. Depending on the workflow, safeguards can include evaluation datasets, confidence thresholds, audit logs, human review, and self-hosted components. Self-hosting a workflow does not by itself keep data out of external model APIs.

faq.question: How much does an engagement cost?
faq.answer: The introductory 15-minute call is free. Diagnostic audits, implementation, and ongoing partnerships are quoted to scope. We agree deliverables, milestones, fees, and the delivery schedule before work starts.

faq.question: What happens after launch?
faq.answer: The scope defines handover and post-launch responsibilities. Ongoing maintenance, improvements, or an embedded technical partnership can be arranged separately, with support coverage and response expectations agreed for your systems.

heading: Notes from the work.
description: Engineering decisions, operational problems, and lessons from building software and AI systems.

title: A content operation with visibility into every AI run
summary: Multi-model content workflows with cost and quality observability.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.
problem: Content production could not keep pace, while output from a single AI model was inconsistent. The team needed an operating platform for content workflows and a way to inspect what each run produced and cost.
contribution: AgileMorph built the content automation platform, combining a Django backend, Celery processing, and a React interface.
solution: Multi-model pipelines bring Claude, GPT, and Gemini into the content-production workflow.
Langfuse observability makes cost and quality visible per run.
Background processing supports the platform’s production workflows.
outcome: The delivered platform brings multi-model content production, background processing, and per-run cost and quality inspection into a single operating workflow.

title: Ask business questions of an existing database
summary: Natural-language search over MSSQL, with ongoing enrichment and classification.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.
problem: Valuable company information lived in a SQL database that only technical staff could query. Business users needed a more accessible way to ask questions of that data.
contribution: AgileMorph delivered a natural-language search tool using MCP over the client’s MSSQL database and continues a related data enrichment engagement.
solution: A plain-language interface gives business users a way to query the existing database.
MCP connects the AI search workflow to the underlying data system.
Related enrichment includes industry-code classification and standardizing LinkedIn job titles at scale.
outcome: The search tool is delivered, making the existing MSSQL database accessible through a natural-language interface. Related classification and enrichment work continues.

title: From WhatsApp listings to structured inventory
summary: Messages, photos, and shorthand become records in Airtable.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.
problem: Inventory listings arrived in unstructured WhatsApp messages, including photos and shorthand. Someone had to read those messages and re-enter the details.
contribution: AgileMorph delivered the intake pipeline and later re-engineered buffering and batching behavior that was driving excessive AI token costs.
solution: Claude extracts structured listing information from incoming messages.
Self-hosted n8n coordinates record creation in Airtable and message forwarding where needed.
The later engineering work addressed token-cost problems caused by buffer and batching bugs.
outcome: The delivered pipeline turns informal messages into structured inventory records and forwards messages where needed. A subsequent engineering engagement corrected buffering and batching bugs behind excessive token usage.

title: A clearer way for wholesale customers to order
summary: A Shopify-based B2B ordering experience, reporting, and developer handover.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.
problem: Wholesale orders arrived through email and manual back-and-forth. The brand also lacked reporting on wholesale performance.
contribution: AgileMorph delivered a B2B wholesale ordering experience using Shopify and SparkLayer, alongside automated reporting.
solution: SparkLayer supplies the B2B ordering layer on the existing Shopify foundation.
n8n and Airtable support the reporting workflow.
A full developer handover document gives the client’s team the information needed to own the system.
outcome: The brand received a wholesale ordering platform, automated reporting, and a full developer handover document for its team to operate the system.

title: Support automation that can act on a ticket
summary: Cancellation and refund automation with evaluation gates and transaction safeguards.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.
problem: Subscription cancellations and refunds required manual support work. Automating them involved both understanding the ticket and safely executing billing actions.
contribution: As a Senior AI Engineer on an independent engagement, Kaustumbh built the support agent, API tool calling, and evaluation setup.
solution: The agent reads tickets and calls subscription, cancellation, and refund APIs.
Idempotency keys and existing-refund checks guard against duplicate refunds. Cancellation and refund are separate steps, with failed refunds retried and unresolved cases routed to a person.
Refunds above $500 and low-confidence classifications go to human review.
CI evaluations combine an intent golden set, LLM-judged responses, and human-labelled refund decisions.
outcome: The resume reports a 45% reduction in manual work on these cancellation/refund tickets. Intent classification reached 98% on a held-out set of 786 labelled tickets; this is an evaluation result, not a guarantee for other workflows.

results.label: Less manual work on cancellation/refund tickets
Intent accuracy on 786 held-out labelled tickets

title: Rules that help analysts review provider documents
summary: A healthcare document rule engine and an interface for review exceptions.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.
problem: Healthcare-professional documents required a manual review step. Analysts needed automated checks and a clear view of the violations that still required attention.
contribution: During an independent Senior Software Engineer engagement, Kaustumbh built the business rule engine and the dashboard interface showing rule violations.
solution: Java, Quarkus, and GraalVM power the rule engine.
A React/TypeScript/Next.js interface makes rule violations visible in the internal dashboard.
The work handled provider PHI within CertifyOS’s HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance program; these are client-program credentials, not AgileMorph certifications.
outcome: The resume reports approximately an hour saved per analyst per day and roughly 20% higher throughput. These figures describe this engagement.

title: An AI coaching product that remembers context
summary: User discovery, contextual memory, voice sessions, and tool-connected coaching.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.
problem: A relationship-coaching product needed relevant history to carry across conversations, reducing repeated context gathering and supporting more complete sessions.
contribution: As a Forward Deployed Engineer, Kaustumbh worked with the founders on user discovery and built memory and voice capabilities into the product.
solution: Conversation embeddings are stored in pgvector on Supabase and tagged by topic. Retrieval is scoped per user and relationship, then filtered before vector search.
The coaching agent connects memory, summaries, reminders, and human escalation through tool calling and MCP integrations.
Voice sessions use VAPI, with FastAPI and React/Next.js supporting the application.
PostHog product analytics and Langfuse prompt evaluations support iteration.
outcome: The resume reports roughly 70% fewer repeated context-gathering turns and about a 30% relative increase in session completion, measured through PostHog. These are product-specific results.

title: Software delivery with a leaner cloud footprint
summary: Manufacturing application backend delivery and AWS optimization.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.
problem: A textile manufacturing application needed backend engineering from design through delivery. Its cloud setup also had opportunities to improve API performance and resource use.
contribution: On an independent Senior Software Engineer engagement, Kaustumbh built backend systems and reworked the AWS setup.
solution: Backend delivery used Python, Django, FastAPI, and MySQL.
Infrastructure changes improved load balancing.
Under-used instances were removed to reduce unnecessary cloud spend.
outcome: The resume reports APIs running 20% faster and an AWS bill 43% lower following the infrastructure changes. These figures apply to that application and setup.

title: Referral tracking and rewards
summary: A delivered referral program captures referrals, tracks progress, and sends rewards through the company’s existing field-service tools.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.

title: Registration and waitlists inside Salesforce
summary: A delivered Salesforce system replaces manual program registration and waitlist handling.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.

attribution: Built by AgileMorph. Presented as portfolio experience; the public reference does not identify a client engagement.

title: Emergency website remediation
summary: Cleared a self-healing WordPress malware chain during an overnight remediation engagement.
attribution: Delivered by AgileMorph Solutions.

title: Phone and SMS assistance for pharmacies
summary: Kaustumbh contributed an AI phone/SMS assistant and authentication and early features for a pharmacy dashboard.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.

title: A code-generation product with usage billing
summary: Kaustumbh built agent tooling, metered credits with Stripe, authentication, administration, and deployment infrastructure.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.

title: Software for bank-led insurance sales
summary: Kaustumbh contributed policy recommendations, applications, and customer management within the client’s SOC 2 and data-protection controls.
attribution: Work delivered by Kaustumbh Jaiswal during a previous independent client engagement. Presented as prior team experience.

title: A retail website and WhatsApp sales agent
summary: A Next.js website rebuild, WhatsApp AI sales agent, and domain migration for a pre-owned luxury watch retailer.
attribution: Prior work delivered through Quido. Presented as team experience; no completed transfer of the engagement to AgileMorph is implied.

title: Measuring visibility in AI search
summary: A phased system measures supplier mentions against a database of 500,000 verified US industrial companies and produces category/state visibility reporting.
attribution: An AgileMorph engagement currently in development.

title: Research-led outbound workflows
summary: An AI research and writing engine drafts personalized outreach into the existing CRM for human review, alongside targeting and sending setup.
attribution: An AgileMorph engagement currently in progress.

title: A specification for multi-outlet operations
summary: Specified five operational flows and six KPIs for a four-brand group, plus a WhatsApp commerce scope. This is specification work, not a delivered platform.
attribution: Specification completed by AgileMorph. Implementation is not presented as delivered.

title: An enriched lead service design
summary: Designed an enriched lead service. The reference does not establish a delivered implementation.
attribution: Service design by AgileMorph. Implementation is not presented as delivered.

title: A continuing product and automation team
summary: An active 12-month technical partnership. Included as an engagement-format example, not a separate quantified outcome.
attribution: An active AgileMorph technical partnership.

children.text: Every agency that pitches new business does prospect research before the first call: pulling domain metrics, checking rankings, sizing up the market, scanning the site for gaps. Prospect research automation promises to compress that work from an afternoon of open browser tabs into a few minutes of setup. Most agencies still do the research by hand, because the job touches five separate systems and no single vendor sells all five. This piece looks at what actually gets automated, what the enrichment platforms leave for you to do anyway, and where the real friction sits: not inside any one tool, but in the gap between them.
What Prospect Research Automation Actually Means

Prospect research automation pulls a prospect's domain data, competitive position, and business context into one place on its own, instead of a rep checking Ahrefs, Semrush, the website, and LinkedIn one tab at a time. Done well, it turns a research pull that used to take half an hour into a profile that updates itself before every call.

In practice that means domain rating, organic traffic direction, ranking keywords, backlink volume, the tech stack a site runs on, and any public signal worth flagging: a funding round, a leadership change, a rebrand. An account executive used to spend a morning before a pitch assembling this by hand. A system built for it assembles the same profile once, automatically, for every prospect that enters the pipeline.
The Real Cost of Manual Prospect Research

The manual version isn't slow because any single step is hard. Pulling a domain report from Ahrefs takes two minutes. Pulling the same view from Semrush takes another two. Checking the site by hand, reading the About page, and skimming recent LinkedIn posts adds ten more. None of that is difficult work. It's work that has to happen again for every prospect, done by a person who could be selling instead.

body.caption: Every step works on its own. Rebuilding the join by hand is what costs the time.
body.title: The manual research pull

children.text: The pattern shows up at agencies of every size: a rep with several tabs open, none of them talking to each other, assembling one prospect's profile from parts that were never meant to be joined by hand. We've seen it directly at a North American marketing agency with 50+ staff, where prospect research had been done by hand in Ahrefs and Semrush for every account entering the pipeline. Nothing about the tools was wrong. The problem was that pulling them together was somebody's job, every time, for every prospect.
What the Enrichment Platforms Solve, and What They Skip

A wave of platforms now sell exactly this: feed in a domain, get back contact data, buying signals, and a scored profile. That's a real improvement over a spreadsheet. For an agency landing a handful of new clients a quarter, an off-the-shelf tool on its free or entry tier may be all you need. If your volume is low, don't build anything custom. Add the login and move on.

The gap shows up at volume. Most of these platforms are a new destination, not a bridge to the ones an agency already runs. The profile they generate still needs a manual copy into the CRM, a check against the account list the reporting already tracks, and a handoff to whoever owns outreach. Connecting the systems already in place removes that copy-paste step and scales with the client count rather than the headcount doing the copying.

FAQ
What is prospect research automation?
It's the practice of pulling a prospect's domain metrics, competitive position, and business signals into one profile automatically, instead of a rep checking each source by hand before a call.
What data should an automated prospect profile include?

At minimum: domain rating and traffic direction, ranking keywords, backlink volume, the site's tech stack, and any recent public signal such as funding or a leadership change. What you include should match what your reps already use to qualify a prospect today.
Does prospect research automation replace judgment?
No. It removes the data-gathering step so a rep can spend the saved time on judgment, reading the account, rather than assembling the report on it.
Do small agencies need an enrichment platform?

Not always. If you're pitching a handful of new accounts a quarter, a free-tier tool and a rep typing notes into the CRM will do the job. The case for automation shows up once volume turns the manual version into somebody's full-time task.
Is this the same as lead enrichment?

They overlap heavily. Research builds the profile; enrichment adds contact and outreach data on top of it. Most of the agencies we work with end up using one connected system for both rather than treating them as separate purchases.
